subject.title: [Feature]: Console-free windows dashboard autostart (also without duplicate gateway launch)

question: Should OpenClaw core add an opt-in Windows dashboard opener Scheduled Task to managed setup/uninstall, and what security/lifecycle contract should it use?
rationale: The requested behavior adds a new Windows logon artifact and setup choice, which affects operator startup UX, cleanup ownership, browser/token handling, and security posture; source review can prove the gap but cannot choose the product contract.

options.title: Approve managed opener
options.body: Implement a separate opener-only Windows task with explicit opt-in, health wait, no Gateway lifecycle calls, idempotent update/removal, focused tests, and live Windows proof.

options.title: Defer to manual/PWA paths
options.body: Keep core limited to the managed Gateway task and `openclaw dashboard`, and document manual browser/PWA startup patterns instead of adding another logon artifact.

options.title: Wait for companion-app direction
options.body: Hold this until the Windows companion/onboarding strategy owns automatic dashboard availability as part of a broader native UX.

recommendation.title: Approve managed opener
recommendation.body: Implement a separate opener-only Windows task with explicit opt-in, health wait, no Gateway lifecycle calls, idempotent update/removal, focused tests, and live Windows proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans dashboard readiness, Windows service lifecycle, and setup UX surfaces where this history shows the strongest ownership signal.
